newsitem.title: USA: U.S. T-bond sinks still futher as futures close.
newsitem.headline: U.S. T-bond sinks still futher as futures close.

text.p: Prices of U.S. Treasury securities continued to crumble late in the session, with the benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond diving 2-1/4 points as Chicago futures trading came to a close.
The bellwether issue was off 2-6/32 at 102-4/32 to yield 6.46 percent. The bond had fallen as much as 2-9/32, or just over 2-1/4 points.

"I think this is a temporary correction," said Michelle Colley Laughlin, Treasury market strategist at Prudential Securities Inc. However, she cautioned that the market was not yet positioned for $38.0 billion in fresh supply that the Treasury will dump on the market next week.

In its quarterly refunding effort, the Department will sell $16.0 billion in three-year notes, $12.0 billion in 10-year notes and $10.0 billion in bonds on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of next week, respectively.
Laughlin said she would not be surprised if the bond yield retested the 6.50 area as players jockeyed pre-refunding.

Longer-term, the Prudential analyst called Friday's nosedive a great buying opportunity. "We're going to move toward, on balance, lower yields. The inflation outlook is still excellent, and the (Federal Reserve) is not going to react quite possibly through year-end," she said.
The catalyst for Friday's collapse was a robust report on the nation's manufacturing economy from the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM).

NAPM's diffusion index soared to 58.6 percent in July, its highest since November 1994 when it registered 59.1 percent. The production index printed 64.4, a 9-1/2-year high, and the new orders component hit a three-year peak.
